title: The potential of quantum computers for Particle Image Velocimetry
authors: Philipp Pfeffer, Theo Käufer, Julia Ingelmann, Christian Cierpka, Jörg Schumacher
abstract: Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) is the prime image-processing technique to measure and visualize velocity fields of laminar and turbulent flows. The velocity field vectors are obtained with sub-pixelaccuracy by analyzing cross-correlations, empowered by Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT). Here, we present a quantum algorithm with multidimensional quantum Fourier Transforms, termed Quantum-based PIV (QuPIV), to replace the classical computation of up to millions of velocity vectors. Our end-to-end quantum algorithm includes a novel state preparation, modified amplitude amplification, and the output extraction. We enhance amplitude amplification by a contracted ground-state projector, which allows a significant reduction of the number of gates in the quantum circuit. We justify the end-to-end capability with numerical studies on all stages of the algorithm on both synthetic and experimental data.
summary: This paper presents QuPIV, a novel quantum algorithm designed to accelerate Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) calculations by replacing classical FFT-based cross-correlation with multidimensional Quantum Fourier Transforms. The authors demonstrate the feasibility of this end-to-end process using experimental data, showing that advanced techniques like contracted amplitude amplification can maintain high accuracy for determining fluid velocity fields.
main_problem: The authors propose a quantum algorithm, QuPIV, designed to replace the classical computation required for Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) by leveraging quantum Fourier Transforms.
main_result: The end-to-end quantum pipeline demonstrates feasibility on experimental PIV data, showing that error sources like input preparation and processing can be analyzed individually, with performance comparable to classical methods.
method: The methodology involves an end-to-end quantum circuit utilizing multidimensional Quantum Fourier Transforms (QFTs) for cross-correlation evaluation, coupled with novel state preparation and contracted amplitude amplification techniques.
model_or_system: The application is PIV, a technique used to measure velocity fields in fluid dynamics by analyzing particle image correlations between two frames. The quantum computation operates on the correlation map derived from these images.
key_observables: Velocity vector ($\vec{u} = \Delta\vec{x}/\Delta t$), peak position error (Euclidean norm), and correlation map ($C_{map}$).
important_parameters: Image size ($N$ pixels), overlap percentage, number of amplification queries ($M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to efficiently load image data into qubits and relies on approximations like using binary inputs (sparsification) and analyzing error sources separately.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the QuPIV workflow from input images to velocity calculation; one figure compares quantum, classical, and analytical solutions for PIV challenge data, while another details individual error source analysis (input, output, processing).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, outlines the end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline (state preparation $ightarrow$ QFT $ightarrow$ Amplitude Amplification), presents theoretical and numerical studies on synthetic/experimental data, and concludes with detailed error analysis.
why_interesting: While focused on fluid dynamics, the core methodology—developing complex, multi-stage quantum algorithms for signal processing using advanced techniques like contracted amplitude amplification—is highly relevant to developing general quantum computational primitives applicable across physics domains.
